head: 4b382e5388e652308d2beca448666630ba6c332d
summary: Check lookups now preserve gh failures and available HTTP status when failed commands return empty stdout. Reported verification supports the small maintenance cost, while live rate-limit behavior and realized user benefit remain unobserved.
reasons: The change addresses issue #656 directly: agents and maintainers receive a gh failure with available HTTP status instead of a misleading JSON error. Scope stays within check lookup handling and focused tests.

Reported evidence includes a reproduction that failed before the fix, passing focused tests, 3454 passing tests, clean RuboCop, and a live missing-PR lookup. This is proportionate to a diagnostic change on an already-failing path; a revert restores the previous behavior without persistent effects.

One review round produced only the untested empty-stdout exit-8 case. Maintenance adds a small error helper and status propagation without new dependencies, configuration, or instructions. Instruction-growth and loading criteria are therefore inapplicable.

A live rate limit, empty stdout with exit 8, and end-to-end diagnostics through pr watch, handoff, and merge were not reported exercised. GraphQL errors without an HTTP marker still lack status. Incident frequency and realized user benefit remain unknown.
alternative: Keep the bounded fix; further diagnostic expansion can wait for evidence of another failure format.
next_action: Use the existing merge process for this head; no product revision is warranted by the supplied evidence.
